blocked_sentences: II — This Saga gains "{2}, {T}: Create a 0/0 colorless Construct artifact creature token with 'This token gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.'"

needs.what: A token id for "a 0/0 colorless Construct artifact creature token with 'This token gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.'" — suggested id `construct_0_0_c_artifact_buff`. Its printed ability, verbatim, is "This token gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.", which is a static `buff` with `self_only` affects and a counted magnitude: {"kind": "static", "text": "This token gets +1/+1 for each artifact you control.", "effect": "buff", "affects": {"self_only": true}, "power": {"count": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Artifact"], "zone": "battlefield"}}, "toughness": {"count": {"controller": "you", "types": ["Artifact"], "zone": "battlefield"}}} — the token counts itself, so a lone Construct is 1/1.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `reference.token_ids` is a closed list and holds no Construct at all. The nearest colorless artifact creature token is `gnome_1_1_c` (1/1 colorless Gnome artifact creature), which is the wrong size, the wrong creature type and carries no ability; substituting it would print a different card.

needs.what: The ability to grant a non-mana activated ability — one that uses the stack — to a permanent, here the source granting it to itself for the rest of the game. Urza's Saga chapter II hands its own Saga "{2}, {T}: Create a ... token", so the grant must survive on a permanent whose printed ability list never contained it, and `stack.ability_of` must be able to resolve it (608.2: an ability on the stack outlives its source, so an index into the printed list is not enough — the granted ability itself, or a stable handle to it, has to travel with the stack item).
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `grant_ability` is exactly the right op and `grantable_abilities` is exactly the right home — chapter I's "{T}: Add {C}" grant loads today. But `cards/loader/__init__.py` refuses any grantable that is an activated ability which is not a mana ability ("only triggered, mana and static abilities can be granted"), because 605.3a is what makes the mana case safe: a mana ability never uses the stack, so `stack.ability_of` — which resolves an ability off its source's *printed* list — is never asked about one. A granted `{2}, {T}: Create a token` would reach the stack with an index into a list that no longer exists and resolve as some other ability of that permanent. The near misses are all different cards: a printed activated ability on the Saga gated by a lore-counter `condition` leaves chapter II's printed line unclaimed and would let the ability be used the turn the Saga enters (chapter I) and after it is sacrificed by a copy effect; `grant_keyword` grants keywords only; and a chapter II that simply creates one token is a one-shot where the printed card is a repeatable outlet.

notes:
Two blockers, not one — the Construct token is the cheaper of them, but closing it alone does not unblock the card, because chapter II's grant is also refused by the grantable-ability rule above. Both live in the same printed sentence.

The rest of the card is expressible today and is written out here so only chapter II is outstanding. The card is `{"types": ["Enchantment", "Land"], "subtypes": ["Urza's", "Saga"], "colors": [], "color_identity": []}` with no mana cost; the parenthetical reminder line needs no claim (rule 714 lives in `engine/sagas.py`) and a chapter writes no `trigger`.

That chapter III selector is the faithful reading of "mana cost {0} or {1}" rather than "mana value 1 or less": `not_colors` over all five colours excludes Esper Sentinel ({W}) and every other coloured one-drop artifact, and `x_in_mana_cost: false` excludes Walking Ballista ({X}{X}, mana value 0), which the printed card also cannot find.

When both needs are closed, the expectation to write is the fallback one: chapter I is the only chapter that fires in the sandbox, and it grants a mana ability rather than changing the board, so `{"zone": "battlefield", "battlefield_count": 33, "counters": {"kind": "lore", "amount": 1}}` — the Saga enters with its first lore counter under 714.2b.
